As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ajoy Chawla, Managing Director, Titan Company Limited. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Chawla. Ajoy Chawla: Thank you. Good evening to everybody on the call. Thank you for being part of this. It has been another very fulfilling quarter. We have seen fantastic growth at a consolidated

level across most of our brands and businesses, and all of them clocking in very healthy growths, driven, of course, by a lot of focus on innovation and prioritizing growth over everything else, given the opportunity that India offers. It looks like very exciting times for us, despite it being a very volatile quarter in terms of some macros. But overall, a very, very good quarter. With that, I hand over to Ashok, our CFO, to share some opening remarks. Ashok Sonthalia: Thank you, Ajoy. Good evening, everyone. I just thought I will take this opportunity to clarify on particularly two items, so that we all are on same page. One is related to customs duty gains. We continue to, as we spoke after quarter one, this quarter also saw a good amount of customs duty gain, which is estimated at ₹490 crores for quarter two in Titan Jewellery division and ₹46 crores in CaratLane. Normalized margin, once you do adjustment for this, on Titan Jewellery business would be 11.1%. The other thing in jewellery, which we have spoken last time, that a large part of MTM gain of quarter one reversed this quarter, which would impact jewellery margin by

about 60 basis points. And if you normalize for that, then TMZ, which is Titan Jewellery business margin, would be 11.7%. Another important item, which is rather new on our P&L, on the face of P&L we have disclosed it separately, is related to liability towards the second tranche for the Damas acquisition. This amount is ₹671 crores. As per Ind AS 109, any financial liability has to be fair valued at every accounting period. And with the current environment, when we looked at our liability at the end of four years, which was accounted for in our books of accounts at ₹1,668 crores, the reassessed liability is less by ₹671 crores. Please note that this assessment will happen at the end of every quarter, and depending on the recovery trajectory of the Damas, there could be pluses and minuses on account of this. But we will continue to disclose it separately so that everyone can understand the nature of that number, and all other performance metrics are looked at normalizing for this adjustment. Titan Company Limited November 05, 2026 continue to certainly believe in the long-term opportunity that Damas represents, and we believe as soon as the geopolitical environment and the conflict situation improves, all the investments are in place to ensure that that long-term opportunity gets realized at the Titan group level. With that, I will open the floor for questions, and we will be very happy to answer. All of us are here to answer your questions. Thank you. Moderator: Thank you very much, Sir. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. The first question is from the line of Videesha Sheth from Ambit Capital. Please go ahead. Videesha Sheth: Hi. My first question was on domestic jewellery EBIT margin. In case of Tanishq, Mia and Zoya, you have talked about investments going to higher competition. So which price points or categories or regions is this persisting in? When you talk about investments, are there any incremental schemes beyond the 0% deduction on old gold, or is it more from an ad campaign perspective? Just in continuation to this, even CaratLane has seen pressure on margins from 10.2% in the base period to 6.5%. Does the same competition argument apply there

from the challenger daily wear brand, or has it got to do with the festive shift? That would be my first question. Ashok Sonthalia: So, let me take this question and then maybe Arun and Saumen can add to that. I am Ashok here. Since increase in customs duty, the domestic market has been operating at a discount compared to international. I am talking about gold prices. That leads to the gold price realization pressure. We also must understand that this is the second, the other side of the coin. One side is the customs duty gain of ₹490 crores, and this pressure is the other side of the coin. So we are normalizing that gain completely, and we are talking this in isolation. Actually, we should look at both sides of the coin, that we are gaining on customs duty, but there is certainly pressure on gold price realization because the entire market is doing that. As far as CaratLane is concerned, they have making a conscious choice to invest on brand building and some of the talent-related investments. And of course, the promotional offers, etcetera, were at elevated level in this quarter. But if you look at the

entire H1 margin profile of CaratLane, still remains healthy, still remains as per our plan that gradually their EBIT margin should start inching up from 8% to 9%, and then further from there in next couple of years. But anything, Arun, Saumen, you want to add? Saumen Bhaumik: No, I am done. Ashok Sonthalia: Yes. Yes. No, so that is what, if I do not know whether… Videesha Sheth: Got it. No, that answers. And the second one is if you can share your observations on the secondary and consumer level trends during this festive versus last festive across all your consumer segments? Page 3 of 17 Sensitivity: Internal Titan Company Limited November 05, 2026 Arun Narayan: Okay, Arun here. I will start with Tanishq, Mia, Zoya. This year festive pretty much can be seen in three phases. The first phase of Navratri from October 11 to October 22, then the second phase in between, and now we are in the last leg with Dhanteras tomorrow. The first phase of Navratri, we saw good consumers, positive consumer sentiments and good traffic to our stores. Pretty much from the day of Vijayadashami for the next few days, there was some softness

owing to gold rate volatility, which kept customers away. But pretty much from the last weekend, which was October 31, we have seen customers come back as we saw an alltime low perhaps of the last many months, last weekend. At an overall level from the start of the festive season till today, gold is kind of softer, which is bringing back customers in, and we hope to see a pretty strong ending to the season over the next few days till November 10. So a very strong start, a very expected strong ending, but a few days in between that were a little soft. On the qualitative side, I think it has been a good run on studded jewellery sustains. As you recall, this began for us pretty much the start of this calendar year. So we have seen three quarters of good studded growth, which continues during the festive as well. And overall, so far, there has been a greater demand for adornment and greater demand for core jewellery, while there is the softness on coins and investment buying, which began in quarter two, which we saw towards August and September. We see that sustaining during festive as

well. Although we see the peak of investment buying in the last few days. So we could see perhaps some greater interest today, tomorrow, and through the weekend. But so far, it seems like a soft interest in investment buying and a greater interest in buying studded and gold jewellery. Saumen Bhaumik: And just to add from CaratLane, during the 24 days of festive season, we, barring for one week, I think we have seen a very healthy growth in terms of both revenue as well as buyer growth. Videesha Sheth: Thanks for that. I will get back in the queue. Ajoy Chawla: Eyewear is not driven by festive. Videesha Sheth: Yes. Wanted to check, in the interim, we did take some initiatives around light weighting, lower cartages, etcetera, when gold price was going up. 14-carat in Tanishq studded jewellery and up to nine-carat in Mia. And so far, it has built a good catalogue and a good availability across stores in the last 9 to 10 months, and it is growing at a very fast clip, and we are seeing good adoption by customers, both in traditional gold, 18-carat, as well as studded jewellery in 14-carat. Obviously, there is a geographic skew to that, and some geographies are adopting much faster, like the North and the West. But overall, very happy with the way the customer response has been to lower cartages. Light weighting, I think, has been there for the last two to three years. In fact, ever since COVID, we have been kind of focusing on making jewellery more accessible, and that has been an ongoing trend. And we are also adding things like detachables and multiple ways of wearing jewellery through modularity. So, many things that are ongoing, but the results are quite satisfactory. Devanshu Bansal: Sure. Sir, my question was, can we think of reversing these initiatives? Because now the gold price benefit will be relatively lower, and maybe we need to sort of increase volume. Is there any thought

process around going back to 22-carat sort of jewellery? Arun Narayan: No, I think as a market leader, the objective is to give choices to customers and leave it to customers as to what to buy. We have a very good assortment of 22-carat. Whatever we have done is without really compromising the core of Tanishq, and it is really an add-on choice. And I think that is the fundamental role of a retailer, to give choice to customers and then allow customers to choose what is in their interest. I do not think we are trying to navigate the ship based on short-term movements. I think in the long run, it will help us be accessible, it will help us gain customer share, help us gain buyer growth. So, it is a strategic tool which we think will give us a greater customer preference, and therefore not something to kind of chop and change based on movements in gold rate. It is a long-term strategic decision we have taken, and we would like to stick with it. Page 5 of 17 Sensitivity: Internal
